requiredFindings.title: The declarativeness prohibition still requires every imperative member to surface as POLICY.IMPERATIVE_KEY_REFUSED
requiredFindings.failureScenario: Forbidden substitutes, Declarativeness, still forbids an imperative member or a string expression from surfacing as any detail other than POLICY.IMPERATIVE_KEY_REFUSED. Item 7 row 4 maps a bundled item 6.2 failure to operational-failed, exit 4, SYSTEM.OUTCOME.ILLEGAL_STATE, host-invariant, detail HOST.INVARIANT_VIOLATED, subject pack:<packId>. The new types-and-codes bullet forbids that bundled member from surfacing as row 3, and row 3 is the row whose detail is POLICY.IMPERATIVE_KEY_REFUSED. Item 10 requires a bundled exec key to give row 4. The public result row 4 requires is a result the declarativeness bullet forbids. Required: scope the declarativeness bullet to a document the caller presents, so that document surfaces as row 3 with detail POLICY.IMPERATIVE_KEY_REFUSED and the member's pointer. A bundled imperative member surfaces as row 4.

scope: Law X12 r2. r1 RF-1 is closed on the rows: a bundled item 6.2 failure is row 4, and row 3 is a caller document. r1 RF-2 is closed: X12-0 widens CONFIG.INVALID before X12b, and the code stays CONFIG.INVALID. RF-1: the declarativeness prohibition still requires every imperative member to surface as POLICY.IMPERATIVE_KEY_REFUSED. No product cargo.
